accuracy.evidence: Every calculation checked by hand and in the lab code: 8 + 2 = 10 and 10 + 3 = 13 (two of the five counters fill the frame, three go on); stem-sentence gaps 2, 3, 3, 13; 15 − 6 = 9 on the 15-cube bar (9 orange, 6 blue, so the cut lands at 9); 7 + 7 = 14 and one more is 15, matching 8 + 2 = 10, 10 + 5 = 15; slips: 6 take away 3 leaves 3 (so 7 + 6 = 13), 7 is 5 and 2 not 5 and 1 (so 15 − 7 = 8), 6 + 7 is one more than 12 (13). Curriculum wording checked against the NC 2013 aims ('reason mathematically… developing an argument, justification or proof using mathematical language') and Year 2 ('recognise and use the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction and use this to check calculations'). Parameterised items checked at range corners: p2 b − 1 (b 2..9), p3 a (a 5..12, b 2..6), m2 b − 2 (b 3..9), m6 2d + 1 (d 3..9).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented KS1 reasoning errors (NCETM mastery materials on make ten, near doubles and stem sentences; NRICH 'convince me' guidance): giving only the answer or 'I just knew' (step 2 prediction, challenge tags loud/again, sorter visual, m1); thinking all 5 or the leftover 3 fill the ten (step 1 prediction, GAPWHY for 3 and 5); checking with the wrong operation, 15 + 6 or 9 − 6 (step 3 prediction, tags plus/whole, m4); believing a second method can give a different right answer (step 3/4 outcome, tags big/first, p4); near doubles one out, 14 or 16 for 7 + 8 (step 4 prediction and pickSum feedback, tags dbl/dbl7, m6); partitioning wrongly (Zoe's '7 is 5 and 1', m3 '6 is 3 and 2'); and trusting a tidy last line instead of checking each step (step 5 prediction, three slip rounds, p5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagexplain is about justifying an answer: bridge 8 + 5 through ten, then put that strategy into a stem sentence, then justify a result two different ways (cut 6 off a 15-cube bar with a draggable line for the inverse; set aside the extra cube of 7 + 8 for a near double), then find the faulty line in worked examples. flagshowwk (ages 5-6) draws 3 + 4 and 7 − 2 and hops a number line; I removed an early counting-on step and a drawing-match step from this lab because they overlapped it. flagcheck checks your own work, flagjustify justifies equation steps for ages 14-16. 6-shingle similarity is at most 1.7% (flag_showwk.js and flag_nline.js) against every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea before the text names it: dropping counters shows the frame is full after 2 ('8 + 2 = 10. 3 are left'), and the next step turns that into words, with a wrong tile explained ('8 + 3 is 11, not 10'); dragging the red cut line shows 'left' and 'taken' counts live, and stopping at 9 left makes the inverse visible before 'take-away undoes adding' is said; moving the extra cube leaves two matching rows (7 + 7 = 14) and the learner has to add it back; in the slip rounds a correct step gets 'is right, check the next step', so the learner checks line by line.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: how many of the 5 fill the frame ('3' or '5'; the frame fills after 2); a good explanation is 'just the answer, 13' or 'I just knew it' (the sentence needs each step); to check 9 + 6 = 15 work out '15 + 6' or '9 − 6' (only cutting 6 from 15 gets back to 9); 7 + 7 = 14 so 7 + 8 is '14' or '16' (the set-aside cube makes 15); to find a mistake 'guess a new answer' (only checking each step finds the three slips).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct wrong-answer messages in why(), each naming the slip: loud (saying it louder does not show it), again (writing it again is not a reason), plus (adding again makes it bigger; to undo + 5 take 5 away), whole (start from the whole, 17), dbl (12 is 6 + 6, so one more), dbl7 (14 is 7 + 7), big (bigger is not more right), first (the first try can have a slip), ans (an explanation shows how you know), fing (any clear way is fine), stop (10 is only half way), add (take away makes it less than 14). The stem-sentence, take-away and near-double steps add their own per-choice messages (GAPWHY, letGo, pickSum).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience (kid and adult readability within limits). Ages 6-7 wording: short sentences with everyday words (make ten, left, take away, one more, check), precise terms introduced plainly (explain your reasoning = say how you know; take-away undoes adding; double). Lab sentences are 17-20 px on pale cards; buttons are short (Move one counter, ◀ one more, Check, Step 2, 15).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases, explanation overlap under 12% with every lesson). Kid paragraphs: answer plus how you know; saying steps in order for 8 + 5; checking with take-away and a double; finding a slip by checking each step. Adult paragraphs: NC aims, Y2 inverse statement and key words; named common mistakes; why stem sentences and second methods help; what each lab step does.

mobile.evidence: Before/after Show me screenshots of all six steps on iPhone 13 (390 px) and 360 px Android in light and dark, and desktop. First pass had the stem sentence broken into 5-word fragments that ran under the number tiles at 360 px, a small drawing panel and 13 px slip lines; fixed by setting the explanation as three full sentences on separate cards with the active gap ringed, removing the drawing step, and raising slip lines to 16 px. Ten-frame cells are about 49 px on phones, number tiles at least 50 px tall, the cut line takes a drag anywhere near the bar, and control buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: 'Move one counter into the ten frame', 'Put 2 in gap 1', 'Take one more cube away' / 'Take one fewer cube away' / 'Check the take-away', 'Set the extra cube aside' then '7 + 8 is 15', 'Step 2 is wrong: …'; challenge answers are 'Answer: …' buttons. narrate() updates the canvas aria-label and the visible narration after every action (e.g. '9 left, 6 taken away.'). walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes, no console errors. Canvas words are dark ink on pale cards in both themes; frame and bar outlines use the theme line colour.
